# DAVID HETTINGER

National Accounts Leadership | Commercial Strategy & Pricing

Denver, CO | 607-239-0128 | 13dmh33@gmail.com | linkedin.com/in/dave-hettinger-12662a52

Open to relocation for the right opportunity

---

## PROFILE

National accounts leader who has spent nearly two decades building, growing, and defending large commercial partnerships — and who now sits on the pricing and margin approval side of the table as well. Built a multi-million-dollar vertical segment from zero, rebuilt a major retail partnership after a failed onboarding by recognizing an execution ceiling and pivoting the model rather than forcing the original plan, and closed the largest single purchase order on a national accounts team. Pairs account-ownership instincts with direct experience in contract structuring, rebate design, and price approval authority — the rare operator who has been on both sides of the negotiation.

## AREAS OF EXPERTISE

National Account Management & Growth · Channel Strategy & Pivot Execution · Contract Negotiation (NDA / MSA / MPA / SOW) · Rebate Structuring & Administration · Cross-Functional Stakeholder Alignment · Pricing & Margin Governance · Forecasting & Revenue Planning · Executive Reporting

## PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

### DAIKIN COMFORT TECHNOLOGIES / MOTILI — Denver, CO
$250M business unit within Daikin, the world's largest HVAC manufacturer.

**Sr. National Accounts Manager — Retail & Multifamily** — 2016 – Jan 2025

- Promoted to Sr. NAM in recognition of segment growth and account complexity. Owned a ~$45M retail segment spanning big-box and online channels alongside the multifamily portfolio.
- Lowe's: grew the account from ~$4M to ~$8M annually after inheriting a failed onboarding during the A2L refrigerant transition. Launched across 300 stores, hit structural execution limits, consolidated to 50 stores, then pivoted to an online SOS channel model — producing a durable $7–10M account within a ~$45M retail segment.
- Launched Lowe's in-store installation services, generating $1.7M in first-year and $2.5M in second-year revenue and establishing a net-new revenue stream with no prior operational model to follow.
- Built the multifamily segment from zero, personally carrying ~$6M in annual sales at peak within a segment that reached $10–12M. Accounts included Greystar, Aimco, Cardinal Group, and Life Storage.
- Closed a $1.4M electrification project with Cardinal Group — the largest single purchase order on the national accounts team.
- Designed an asset tagging system during the refrigerant transition to track installed equipment across properties — preserving revenue continuity through a disruptive product change and giving the team the first systematic view of the installed base.
- Negotiated and managed complex commercial agreements across the portfolio including rebate structures, volume commitments, and channel exclusivity terms.
- Managed accounts spanning the U.S. and Canada, navigating cross-border commercial and pricing considerations.

**Manager of Sales Planning** — Feb 2025 – Mar 2026

- Owned business unit forecasting, quota and commission design, and rebate structures across the national accounts portfolio.
- Managed contracts through negotiation and post-execution administration — NDA, MSA, MPA, SOW, and rebate agreements — serving as the commercial bridge between sales intent and financial terms.
- Led Salesforce rollout and administration; built reporting in DOMO and Tableau to give sales leadership visibility into pipeline health and account-level profitability.
- Managed a team spanning national and key account management, project management, data analysis, and pricing.

**Manager of Finance — Pricing, Margin & Commercial Governance** — Apr 2026 – Present

- Own pricing policy, price approval authority, margin analysis, and rebate management for national accounts and the Motili business unit; deliver executive and investor reporting across Motili, Commercial, and Residential New Construction (~$1.3B combined revenue).
- Built the organization's first price-to-volume governance loop, tying discount approvals to verified volume delivery — producing ~$1.4M in annual sales lift.
- Identified structural pricing inefficiency in the water heater category and executed two price increases in 2026, delivering ~$500K in annual gross margin improvement.
- Co-built an AI-enabled contract review and routing agent with Legal and Finance leadership, cutting initial contract review from 60+ minutes to 1–2 minutes and eliminating a multi-week stakeholder coordination cycle.

## EDUCATION

B.S. Finance, International Business minor — Binghamton University School of Management
Study abroad in negotiation coursework, New Delhi, India

## SYSTEMS & TOOLS

Salesforce, HubSpot, DOMO, Tableau, SAP, PriceFX, Microsoft 365 (advanced Excel), Microsoft Copilot

# Cover Letter

David Hettinger
Denver, CO | 607-239-0128 | 13dmh33@gmail.com

Dear Hiring Manager,

I'm writing to express interest in the Director, National Accounts – Kroger role at Pabst. I want to be direct about what I bring: nearly two decades of national account ownership inside one organization, including building a $10–12M vertical segment from zero, rebuilding a major retail partnership after a failed onboarding by pivoting the channel model rather than forcing a broken plan, and closing the largest single purchase order on my team. I've also spent the last two years on the other side of the table — owning pricing policy, margin governance, and rebate structures for a $250M business unit, which means I understand account economics from both the sales and the approval seat.

What I don't have is direct experience with Kroger, grocery retail, or the beverage alcohol category and its three-tier distribution model. I don't want to overstate that. What I can offer is a proven pattern: taking over a strained or underperforming partnership, diagnosing the real structural constraint, and rebuilding the commercial model around it — plus the contract, rebate, and pricing fluency that a partnership of this size and importance requires.

I'd welcome the chance to discuss how that pattern might translate to the Kroger relationship, and to be candid about where the learning curve would be steepest so we can assess fit honestly together.

Thank you for your consideration.

David Hettinger

Dear Hiring Manager,

I'm writing to express interest in the Director, Distribution Strategy & Business Planning role within MetLife's Group Benefits Regional Business. I recognize this newly created role sits inside an insurance and broker/employer distribution context I have not worked in directly — I want to name that plainly rather than paper over it. What I bring instead is nearly two decades of building the muscle this role clearly needs: sales planning, channel strategy, and the discipline to turn market data into pricing and go-to-market decisions.

As Manager of Sales Planning at a Daikin Comfort Technologies business unit, I built a real-time market share and competitive pricing model for a ~$90M segment that let us hold 40–65% share by adjusting price dynamically as conditions shifted — the same kind of translation from market signal to commercial action that a growth engine on the path from $6B to $8.5B in premium will need. I also inherited a stalled retail account after a failed launch, recognized a structural execution ceiling at 300 stores, and pivoted it to an online channel model that produced a durable $7–10M account — a channel-strategy pivot, not a straight recovery, and I'd tell it that way in an interview.

I now sit on the other side of the table as well, owning pricing policy, margin governance, and rebate structures for a $250M business unit, with executive and investor reporting across a ~$1.3B combined portfolio. That sales-to-finance crossover is uncommon, and it's the lens I'd bring to distribution strategy and business planning: someone who has built the account and someone who has approved the terms.

I'd welcome the chance to discuss how this background maps onto Regional Business's growth plan, and to be candid about where I'd need to ramp on the Group Benefits and broker-channel specifics.

Sincerely,
David Hettinger
